jobs.description: RETIRED / PERMANENTLY DISABLED 2026-07-27 (token-cost cut, Nick) — leave enabled:false. payload.message:
Run the B2B Ads reply scanner.

Scan Gmail for new Muso Ads outreach replies across these accounts: a@muso.ai, f@muso.ai, ak@muso.ai, aaron.k@muso.ai.

For EACH account, run EXACTLY this command (substitute <ACCT>) and do not add or change flags. The flag that includes message bodies in search results is --include-body; do NOT use --body (that is a gmail send flag and will fail with 'unknown flag --body'):

gog gmail messages search 'in:inbox newer_than:1d ("Muso Ads" OR "Muso.AI" OR "calendar.muso.ai" OR "Private invite" OR "820K" OR "ads to 820K" OR "Reaching 820K" OR "Muso.AI x")' --account <ACCT> --max 50 --include-body --json

Read the JSON straight from stdout. Do not write results to temp files and do not pipe through jq. The Gmail search is bounded to the last day (newer_than:1d, the only valid Gmail unit near this window); from the results keep only messages received in roughly the last 70 minutes (the run cadence) by reading each message's date. Do not rely only on label:"B2B - Ads" because inbound replies may not carry the label.

Filter out internal muso.ai mail, SaaS notifications, DMARC reports, newsletters, spam, unrelated customer support, and unrelated inbox noise. Keep true prospect replies, meeting-booking language, referrals/new points of contact, questions, pricing asks, explicit pass/unsubscribe replies, OOO with useful referral info, and B2B delivery failures/bounces. Deduplicate by Gmail threadId and account.

Current B2B outreach rules:
- Gmail owns send/reply detection.
- NocoDB is read-only and is the source of contact/company context. Look up contact/company when possible.
- Do not write to NocoDB.
- Do not use GHL.
- Do not use Google Sheets.
- Do not move stages.
- Do not auto-reply.
- Do not create Gmail drafts.
- Do not mark messages read.

For every true item, classify it as Replied, Meeting Booked, Referral, Pricing, Question, Interested/send-info, Soft-no/later, Pass, Bounce, OOO, or Other.

Then apply the muso-outreach-reply-responder logic:
- Decide answer vs skip.
- Match sender voice to the receiving account: a@/ak@/aaron.k@ = Aaron.
- Pull thread history before drafting if available.
- If answering, provide ONE exact suggested reply whose only goal is a 15-20 minute call.
- Keep warm-thread replies short and playbook-native.
- No em dashes or en dashes.
- Do not create the Gmail draft until Nick or Aaron approves in Slack.

If no actual new B2B prospect replies or B2B bounces are found, final visible message must be exactly: NO_REPLY

If one or more are found, final visible message must be concise Slack mrkdwn for #sales-alerts. For each item:
*New B2B Reply*
From: *<name>* (<company>, <title if known>)
Received on: <account>
Type: *<classification>*
Preview: _<short preview>_
Verdict: answer / skip

*Suggested reply:*
> <exact draft body, as Aaron would send>

Manual next step: Nick/Aaron approve before any Gmail draft is created. Nick/team updates NocoDB Status manually if needed.

Always emit a visible final assistant message. Never end with thinking-only output.

jobs.name: credit-verification-batch-4h
jobs.description: DISABLED 2026-10-11 (firstmate containment; captain: 'we can't let bad credits into the system'): its approve rule approve_owning_track==100 AND total_risk_percent<80 was inverted (100 = the validator's owning-track shortcut did NOT fire), so it approved validator-DECLINED rows. Disabled live on node-8 at 02:26Z; this repo flag keeps deploys from re-arming it. Re-enabling needs the captain's approval recorded in policies/credit-approval-automation.json (CI: scripts/check-credit-approval-automation.sh). Autonomous drain of the unverified-credits queue via the Lobster pipeline. Fires every 4h and runs the dispatcher DIRECTLY as a deterministic command (500-credit FIFO real apply), self-posting the batch summary to #credit-verification (verify-credit-batch-mvp.lobster sets POST_PARENT_TO_CHANNEL=1); see hydra#305. WAS an isolated agent turn until 2026-09-17: that shape reported every run success from the MODEL finishing, so when the dispatch started failing on 2026-09-11 (openclaw 2026.8.x AGENT_SELECTION_REQUIRED: an unowned "main" session key is refused once multiple agents are configured) the cron read ok, consecutiveErrors=0, for six days while ~2.7k declined credits piled up in 'unverified' (firstmate task credit-submissions-stuck-rca-c5). jobs.name: uvn-ticket-popularity-under30
jobs.description: ENABLED 2026-08-13 after Nick authorized the autonomous admin-write gate; PROFILE-SCOPED 2026-09-08 (#914); APPLY MODE + HOURLY from 2026-09-09 after a shadow period whose only settled decision matched the human. Runs at :30 every hour — hourly, not 4-hourly, because the point is to beat the humans' measured 2.2h median wait, which a 4h cadence cannot; :30 keeps it clear of the credit-verification batch at :00. A TO DO hydra-action-request/action:credit-verify ticket carrying the automation:uvn-under30 eligibility tag and a UUID profile is in scope (Caroline's recommendation does not gate enrollment — the cron's own policy is the gate); the cron resolves that profile's live user_verification_needed rows from the backend itself (exact ids in the ticket only narrow the scope), fetches authoritative live Spotify popularity, excludes fraud and backend hard-reject signals, atomically approves only rows still in user_verification_needed with popularity below 30, verifies every exact ID, never rejects, and resolves the ticket only when the profile has nothing left in verification; rows it cannot approve are listed on the ticket for the human reviewer. REVERSAL BREAKER: before writing anything it re-reads every request it approved in the last 14 days, and if more than UVN_MAX_REVERSALS of them are no longer approved it halts the run and asks for a human — a person undoing our approval is the one direct signal the sub-30 rule was wrong, and humans reversed 0 of 127 of their own approvals beforehand. It fails closed when that history cannot be read. --limit caps approvals per run, --mode shadow reverts to recording only, and /etc/hydra/uvn-under30-cron.disabled silences it. Plain-English summaries are announced to #credit-verification by the cron runner; policy mismatches are de-enrolled once and remain open for manual review without turning the run into a recurring command-failure alert.

jobs.name: credit-approval-auditor-hourly
jobs.description: APPROVAL AUDITOR (captain 2026-10-11: 'need a monitor that closely watches credit approvals on our side to check if they should have been given ... with AI and internet searches'). Hourly at :45 it re-checks every credit request APPROVED in the last 90 minutes (or since the previous successful run, minus 15 minutes, if that is earlier - at most 24h back; an older gap is alerted as 'N minutes not audited'; approvals are recorded oldest first in chunks, no chunk or model batch starts past an 1800s deadline (a chunk starts only if the longest one so far still fits) so alerts are always printed, and an early stop alerts and resumes from the last finished chunk), by any path (validator, admin queue, any job). Catalog evidence (Spotify/Tidal/MLC/Jaxsta raw credits) runs for every approval. PHASE A (now): catalog-only - every approval is checked against the trusted sources and the identity/velocity/approver signals, no model calls. PHASE B (once the captain tops up OpenRouter, by creating /etc/hydra/credit-review-model.enabled on node-8): the model with web search (Discogs, AllMusic, label/liner notes, trade press; the claimant's own sites and profiles and user-generated platforms such as Instagram/SoundCloud/Bandcamp/Wix/Blogspot never count as evidence) runs for 100% of big tracks (catalog track popularity >= 60, any track artist >= 90, or either unknown) and a stable 10% sample of the rest, capped at $2 per run, skipped entirely while the shared OpenRouter balance is under the floor in the design doc (one 'CREDIT-AUDIT NOTE' per day says so), and $8 per UTC day (measured ~$7/day at full coverage on grok-4.3: ~47 big-track approvals/day + 10% of ~3,100 others, minus the ones the catalog already decides). Verdicts CONFIRMED / SUSPECT / CONTRADICTED / UNVERIFIABLE go to /var/lib/hydra/credit-review/ledger.sqlite3. Stdout (announced to #credit-verification) is one 'CREDIT-AUDIT ALERT:' line per CONTRADICTED big-track credit (also queued for human re-review) and per approver-identity problem (agent-hydra-main / admin_u / unknown approver, or a validator-declined row approved with no recorded approver), plus one per-profile burst alert naming the profile when one profile has >= 10 SUSPECT/CONTRADICTED or >= 20 approvals within 2h (re-alerted only when the profile has approvals newer than its last alert); a quiet run prints only NO_REPLY and posts nothing, logs go to /var/lib/hydra/credit-review/run.log, never stderr. READ-ONLY on credits: GETs only, never removes or changes a credit. Kill switch: /etc/hydra/credit-review.disabled. Design: docs/credit-verification/ai-credit-reviewer.md.

jobs.name: credit-trust-verify-notify-15m
jobs.description: TRUST YET VERIFY user notes for NEW provisional approvals (captain 2026-10-15 22:12Z, verbatim: "i want AI live now - we have too many credits to approve and to get supporting data for - let users know where there was a credit given and that it needs support (trust yet verify approach)"; 23:40Z: "if no valid verification comes it should be removed", kept for new credits on 2026-10-16 00:35Z). SHIPPED enabled:false: enable only after Fable approves the windowed copy and the PR that flips LIVE_WINDOWED_COPY_APPROVED in scripts/intercom-verify-request.sh lands; until then the gate refuses every real verify-live send, so no new credit is ever told "nothing changes". Every 15 min at :07/:22/:37/:52, after credit-trust-decide-15m, it reads the decider ledger (/var/lib/hydra/credit-review/ledger.sqlite3: decision_outcomes action='approve' AND outcome='approved', joined to decisions, the same query as decide.run_approvals), RE-READS each row from the admin API (GET only) and keeps only rows the server says are approved now, groups them by the credit request's account, and sends ONE Intercom email per account per UTC day through the gate: Caroline identity pinned, Fable's fixed windowed copy ('We added your {role} credit on "{track}". Please help us verify it', ONE date, the reply-by date 30 days out ('it will be removed from your profile after that day'), a restore line; N-credits digest variant), HTML-escaped fields, leak check, exactly one Intercom user by account email, api-log before the POST, response verified after, each request id notified at most once (verify-ledger claim written before the POST; an unknown outcome is never re-sent). It also sends the day-14 and day-25 reminders of those notes and tags replies WITH attachments from that user 'credit-proof' (tag only: no reply, no decision, the reply text is never read); ANY reply from that user (text or attachment, author only) holds the note's credits from removal for a human and is reported in the run summary. `credit-review.py verify-notify --removal-due FILE` exports, per credit, the credits from the day after their note's reply-by date with no ACCEPTED document (review per credit with --proof-review MESSAGE_ID --request-ids ... --outcome accepted|rejected, a rejection with a fixed --reason when a document was received; each rejected credit gets ONE after-rejection note of its own (the reason, or 'we still need a document' after a reply with no document; a reply-by date at least 7 days out) and is removal-due only after the date that note named; a user reply after that note holds the credit for a human) for the guarded removal step, and writes the credits held for a human (document awaiting review, user reply, rejection not yet explained) to FILE.held, never to FILE; nothing is removed here and it never writes a credit-request status. A run with nothing to do prints NO_REPLY; a gate failure exits non-zero. Kill switch: /etc/hydra/credit-verify-notify.disabled (or enabled=false here). DOCUMENTS ALREADY ON FILE ARE NEVER ASKED FOR (captain standing order "make sure you arent asking for things from users that already submitted documents and we approved. dont piss anyoen off"): per CREDIT for new credits, in the note and its reminders: a credit with its own entry on /var/lib/credit-trust/proof-on-file.json (any kind) or approved by a person is not asked about; a user with a pending_doc on another credit waits: nothing is sent or closed, each held-back credit gets a deferred_pending_doc row in the verify ledger (no daily message, never removal-due) that every later run re-reads whatever its age (and while a rejected send of it has retries left), and the user gets one batched windowed ask once that document is reviewed; a generic Intercom attachment is no reason to skip a new credit. A missing, >3h-old or incomplete list (sources[] must name every required part, each fresh; users must match entries) means zero asks that run and a non-zero exit. `--removal-due FILE` leaves out credits with their own proof-on-file entry (any kind) or a human approval, and on a missing or stale list exports nothing and exits non-zero.

jobs.name: credit-past-verify-wave-15m
jobs.description: PAST-CREDIT DOCUMENTATION ASK, genuine risk only. Captain 2026-10-15 23:35Z (verbatim): "im referring to before when nick made changes and did a trust verify flow and now we have a lotnof credits to verify with documents and give people 30 days to send something in for the ones missing documents"; narrowed 2026-10-16 00:35Z: "how many credits were approved without documentstion i dont want to lose users unless its obvious fraud feom tbe past" and 02:00Z: "are you annoying people fornbackup that we shpuldnt be?". Every 15 min at :11/:26/:41/:56 it reads the wave file /var/lib/hydra/credit-review/waves/retro-past.csv (the population, built from the retro review's risk tiers; credit_request_id,user_id,profile_id[,track_id,tier,pop_now,paid,claim_date]; NO_REPLY while absent), re-reads each row from the admin API (GET only) and announces only rows still approved, then sends ONE friendly Intercom email per user listing their credits (paid users first, big tracks first; at most 100 users per run and 600 per UTC day, 1s apart) through scripts/intercom-verify-request.sh --campaign retro-past: Caroline pinned, fixed role-specific copy with NO deadline and NO removal language, leak check, api-log and verify-ledger claim before the POST. At most one message per user, ever: no follow-up, and a user who already sent proof (a credit-proof reply on any note) is never asked. Replies with attachments are tagged credit-proof (tag only, no decision). Optional --exclude-users FILE leaves out accounts whose existing credits are handled elsewhere. Past credits are NEVER removed by this path: a non-response leaves the credit in place, and `credit-review.py verify-wave --unverified FILE` exports those as unverified for the board; proven fraud goes through its own take-back path. It never writes a credit-request status. SHIPPED enabled:false and the gate is send-locked (RETRO_COPY_APPROVED=0): enable after Fable's copy GO + the captain's approval land in the PR that flips the lock and the wave file is in place. Kill switch: /etc/hydra/credit-verify-notify.disabled. DOCUMENTS ALREADY ON FILE ARE NEVER ASKED FOR (captain standing order "make sure you arent asking for things from users that already submitted documents and we approved. dont piss anyoen off"): users on /var/lib/credit-trust/proof-on-file.json (any kind) are skipped, a missing or >3h-old list means zero asks that run and a non-zero exit, human-approved requests are never asked about, and the gate skips anyone whose Intercom conversations already hold a user-attached document or a credit-proof tag.

jobs.name: hydra-health-watch-twice-daily
jobs.description: Read-only twice-daily Hydra health check on node-8: gateway units and ports, deploy drift, last Deploy HYDRA run. Posts to Slack so it works when the Mac is down. Does not cover Sentry (MUS-7155, MUS-7136).

payload.message:
Hydra health watch for node-8. Read-only, twice daily. It covers the gateway units, the gateway ports, deploy drift and the last deploy only. It does NOT check Sentry or any Muso app errors, so HEALTHY here is not a prod-wide all-clear.

READ-ONLY RULE: run only the read commands below. Do not restart any service. Do not run deploy.sh, rollback.sh, or any kubectl command that writes. Do not create or change any file on the host. Never use a path under /dev as the target of any command; /dev/null may only be used as a redirect sink.

Run these checks in order with the shell (exec) tool:

1. Gateway units. Run `systemctl is-active openclaw-gateway-main openclaw-gateway-edge` and `systemctl show -p NRestarts -p ActiveEnterTimestamp openclaw-gateway-main openclaw-gateway-edge`. A unit that is not `active` is a failure. Report the NRestarts value and the ActiveEnterTimestamp for each unit. Do not judge a restart yet: check 4 decides it. Deploy HYDRA restarts both gateways on purpose every day at about 04:00 UTC, so a restart on its own is not a failure.

2. Gateway ports. For each of 18789 and 18810, run `curl -s --max-time 10 -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ | tail -c 3`. The last three characters are the HTTP code. Any code that is not 2xx is a failure. `000` means no connection, which is also a failure.

3. Deploy drift. Run `cat /opt/hydra/.deployed-sha` and `gh api repos/Muso-AI/hydra/git/ref/heads/main --jq .object.sha`. Report both shas. If they differ, report that main has moved since the last deploy. This is information, not a failure.

4. Last deploy. Run `gh run list -R Muso-AI/hydra --workflow 'Deploy HYDRA' --limit 1 --json conclusion,status,createdAt,updatedAt,url`. A conclusion of `failure` or `cancelled` is a failure. A status of `in_progress` or `queued` is information. Now judge the restarts from check 1. Convert every timestamp to UTC before you compare. If the run's status is `completed`, a gateway whose ActiveEnterTimestamp is before the run's `updatedAt` was restarted by that deploy: information only. A gateway whose ActiveEnterTimestamp is after the run's `updatedAt` restarted after the last deploy finished: a failure. If the run's status is `in_progress` or `queued`, every restart is information.

Post ONE message in this form:
- All four checks were read and none failed: start with `HEALTHY`, then one line of evidence per check.
- Any check failed: start with `FAILURES`, then one line per failure with its evidence.
- Any check could not be read (command error, empty output, unreachable): add `PARTIAL - <check name> not read` for each one. A run with an unread check is never `HEALTHY`, even if every other check passed.

State facts only. Give no advice. Do not restart or fix anything.

jobs.description: TRUST-YET-VERIFY decider (captain 2026-10-15 ~22:12Z: 'i want AI live now ... trust yet verify approach'; wiring data/credit-trust-system-fable-a1/live-tonight.md Piece 1). Every 15 min, oldest held (unverified) rows first, <= 500 per run: provisional APPROVE only for non-big tracks with no validator conflict and one evidence kind (trusted catalog confirmation, a trusted footprint, or Codex on server-fetched sources with verified quotes on >= 2 independent domains, never crowd-edited MusicBrainz/Wikipedia alone; $0; editorial roles only on trusted catalog confirmation under pop 30), else REQUEST SUPPORT (user_verification_needed - Knock asks the user for proof). Big tracks and the fraud lists are never approved (no named-user rules); paying users' rows are decided first; support requests are never re-sent (proof on file -> hold, a credit asked once ever, one ask per user per 24h, none at all while the proof-on-file export is unknown); a model outage DEFERS rows instead of sending support requests. Every decision is in the decisions table of /var/lib/hydra/credit-review/ledger.sqlite3 before the write (credit-review.py explain <id>; revert --run <id>). Command-shaped: exit code = run status. Registered in policies/credit-approval-automation.json (credit-trust-decide). Kill switch /etc/hydra/credit-trust-decide.disabled.

jobs.name: credit-verify-proof-intercom
jobs.description: Supporting-document forensics, SHADOW (H3; captain's first principle 2026-10-15: proof by email or Intercom, fraud-checked before it counts). Every 30 min: classifies Intercom conversations whose attachment cache changed in the last 2 days (one read-only Intercom GET each) and analyses each new customer attachment of a proof conversation (a file sent after a teammate/bot asked for documentation) in a sandboxed systemd transient unit with no network: file sniff, image provenance/C2PA/AI-generator markers, PDF revisions/fonts/overlays/signatures, OCR content checks, cross-account reuse. Writes only /var/lib/hydra-credit-verify/proof.sqlite (signals with cited regions, hashes, verdicts; no document text). Changes no credit, sends nothing. Kill switch: /etc/hydra/credit-verify.disabled. Docs: docs/credit-verification/proof-forensics.md.

jobs.name: credit-verify-proof-email
jobs.description: DISABLED until the inbound verification address (verify@) exists - credit-trust V2 ticket. Supporting-document forensics for the EMAIL channel, SHADOW (E-IN). Every 10 min: reads raw messages delivered to /var/lib/hydra-credit-verify/inbound-email/new. A message counts only if the trusted receiving MTA authenticated the sender (dmarc=pass or aligned dkim=pass) and the address is the confirmed email of exactly one Muso user (GET /admin/user); its attachments get the same sandboxed forensics as Intercom files (source=email). Spoofed or unknown senders are filed under rejected/ with the reason; nothing is attached or sent.
